name: Net carbs
seoTitle: Net carbs Calculator — Formula, Units & Example
seoDesc: Net carbs: work out sugar alcohol (2) from the total carbohydrates and the fiber. A free health calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: Supply the total carbohydrates, the fiber and the sugar alcohol and the Net carbs calculator solves for sugar alcohol (2). Think of it as a shortcut for an informed starting point to take to a clinician, not a diagnosis. Nothing is submitted anywhere: the arithmetic runs in the page you are looking at.

sections.title: How does the Net carbs calculator work?
sections.html:
The Net carbs calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports sugar alcohol (2) in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case; then you type in the total carbohydrates, the total carbohydrates (2), the fiber (2) and the sugar alcohol.

Press Calculate once and the page holds the relationship, tracking which boxes you filled and working out everything else; from that point on it follows every edit you make.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Net carbs calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Sugar alcohol=(-fiber × are you in the USA or Canada? − net carbohydrates + total carbohydrates) ÷ does your product only contain sugars from either erythritol, xylitol, mannitol or lactitol?
Total net carbohydrates=net carbohydrates × servings consumed
Weight of your product=100 × total net carbohydrates ÷ net carbohydrates
Fiber=(-net carbohydrates − sugar alcohol × does your product only contain sugars from either erythritol, xylitol, mannitol or lactitol? + total carbohydrates) ÷ are you in the USA or Canada?
Total net carbohydrates=(1 ÷ 4) × calories from net carbs

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Net carbs calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Deciding whether a reading is worth a second look
  • Tracking a measurement over time and understanding what changed
  • Preparing for an appointment so you can describe your numbers clearly
  • Any time the same 3 figures keep coming back — the total carbohydrates, the fiber and the sugar alcohol — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Net carbs calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns sugar alcohol (2), derived from the total carbohydrates, the fiber and the sugar alcohol. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Net carbs calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the total carbohydrates, the fiber and the sugar alcohol, which is 11 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (3 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Total net carbohydrates = 100. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Net carbs calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
